upstream_station.location_role: Path B North Avenue approach before the all-approach merge
upstream_station.aggregation: median across duplicate same-year major-station records

merge_station.location_role: immediately upstream of the complete all-approach merge on North Avenue

latest_upstream_corroboration.interpretation: The 2024 upstream AADT is 6.4 percent below the 2018 upstream median and 5.8 percent below the 2022 value. It refreshes the upstream context but does not update station 182001 or measure the full merged flow.

current_public_data_check.scope_note: The absence finding applies to the official 2024 annual AADT file. NJDOT's current Traffic Viewer and Transportation Data Management System should still be searched manually because automated access was blocked during the review.

corridor_operations_cross_check.source_title: Kapkowski Road Corridor Improvements Project Concept Development Report
relevant_findings: North Avenue eastbound at Dowd Avenue had an eastbound right lane group at LOS E in the AM and PM peak hours.
The southbound left/through lane group at North Avenue and Dowd Avenue was LOS E in the PM peak hour.
The southbound left/through lane group at North Avenue and Kapkowski Road/IKEA Drive was LOS E in the PM and Saturday peak hours.
corridor_operations_cross_check.pandemic_adjustment: The engineering team compared 2020 counts with 2018 pre-pandemic ATR data and applied time-period growth factors. Treat the results as adjusted operational evidence, not unmodified 2020 traffic conditions.
corridor_operations_cross_check.interpretation: The study supports peak-period operational stress along the North Avenue corridor but does not supply a newer public AADT value for station 182001.

county_context_cross_check.source_title: Union County Truck Mobility Study Final Report
county_context_cross_check.segment: CR 624 from Earhart Drive to the New Jersey Turnpike overpass
county_context_cross_check.finding: Highest AADT among county roadways listed in the study.
county_context_cross_check.interpretation: Confirms the station's corridor significance and location; does not add a newer count.

secondary_cross_check.source_type: FHWA HPMS attributes in the 2025 NHS release
secondary_cross_check.note: The independent segment dataset supports increasing volume along North Avenue, but it does not match the NJDOT station locations or methods and should not be used to validate the exact 93.9% magnitude.

decision.finding: The North Avenue approach to the common corridor is a historical demand-concentration point: 2018 daily volume immediately upstream of the complete merge was approximately 1.94 times the robust upstream Path B baseline. The 2024 upstream count refreshes the approach context, but no 2024 annual-file record updates station 182001 and the full merged flow remains unmeasured.
decision.operational_implication: Treat the shared North Avenue-to-McLester corridor as the primary traffic-monitoring and contingency-planning zone regardless of which inbound corridor family is chosen.
decision.reason_path_ranking_not_supported: AADT measures volume, not travel-time reliability, queueing, incidents, gate delay, or truck-specific performance.

limitations: AADT is an annualized daily-volume estimate, not an hourly congestion or speed measure.
The 1.94-times comparison is a same-year 2018 historical comparison, not a current traffic estimate.
Station 182001 is immediately upstream of the complete approach merge and is not a true post-merge counter.
The upstream station has nine duplicate 2018 major-station records with unexplained variation; the median is used as a robust summary.
The two NJDOT station types differ: major station versus 48-hour volume station.
Volume added between stations cannot be attributed exclusively to Path A because local access and other ramps may contribute.
The NJDOT dataset does not identify trucks separately in these station records.
The official 2024 annual AADT file contains upstream station 3-3-024 but no station 182001 row; the current NJDOT station system still requires a manual search.
The City of Elizabeth's 2020 counts were collected during the COVID-19 pandemic and adjusted against 2018 pre-pandemic data.
No observed terminal gate queue or service-time data are included.
next_collection: Search NJDOT's current Traffic Viewer and Transportation Data Management System manually for station 182001 and Route 624 milepoint 1.75.
Install a seven-day downstream screenline count immediately after the last approach joins and before McLester/Tripoli or another access point changes the flow.
Install approach counters and merge video so downstream totals can be reconciled to contributing flows and lane-changing or queue conditions.
Collect 15-minute direction, vehicle-classification, truck-share, and speed observations over seven consecutive nonholiday days.
Collect repeated truck travel times by directional approach before the common merge.
Collect North Avenue, McLester Street, and terminal-gate queue/service times separately.
Calculate merged AADT, peak-hour volume, approach contributions, median, p80, p95, buffer time, and planning-time index only after repeated observations exist.

nodes.label: N.J.A.C. 13:18-1.2 — Requirement of permit (NJPASS-hosted rule copy)

record.label: N.J.A.C. 13:18-1.2 — Requirement of permit (NJPASS-hosted rule copy)
source_text: (a) Except as provided in (c) below, a single-trip permit is required for each one-way trip of an oversize or overweight vehicle that exceeds the dimension or weight provisions of N.J.S.A. 39:3-84.
(b) In the event the vehicle is both oversize and overweight, a single-trip permit will be issued for each one-way trip.

(c) An annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit may be issued for a tractor semitrailer combination engaged in the transportation of sealed containers of the type commonly used for the conveyance of freight transportation in international ocean going commerce as follows:

1. Sealed containers transported under an annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit shall bear the seal of the United States Custom Service, the seal of another governmental agency or the seal of a shipper;

2. The combined gross vehicle weight of any tractor semitrailer combination, including load or content conveying sealed containers, shall not exceed 90,000 pounds. The tractor semitrailer combination per-axle combined weight shall not exceed 38,000 pounds for any one tandem axle unit in any tractor semitrailer combination and shall not exceed 56,400 pounds for any tri-axle trailer configuration. Additionally, vehicles shall conform with the axle limitations in N.J.S.A. 39:3-84 and the maximum tire load limit in N.J.A.C. 13:18-1.10(a)2. Vehicles or combination of vehicles that exceed these weight limits may not use an annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit and shall obtain a single-trip permit as described in (a) above;

record.label: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook — 2.1.3.6 Trailers and Semitrailers (N.J.S.A. 39:3-84.a(4))
source_text: As the diagram above shows, the maximum length of a semitrailer shall not exceed 53 feet when operated as part of a combination of vehicles consisting of one motor-drawn vehicle and a drawing or power unit vehicle.

Semitrailers greater than 48 feet in length but not more than 53 feet in length must be transported using the National Network unless seeking food, fuel, rest, repairs or to reach a terminal by the direct route (that is, the shortest travel distance). Upon completing each trip, the large truck should return to the National Network in a manner consistent with reaching its next terminal. Trips off of the National Network or the New Jersey Access Network onto all other local unrestricted roadways should only be for the purpose of accessing a terminal on those roadways, by the shortest distance.

nodes.label: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook — 3.1 Single-Trip OS/OW Permit

record.label: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook — 3.1 Single-Trip OS/OW Permit
record.source_text: A single-trip permit allows a carrier to haul a non-divisible load above legal size and/or weight limitations and is valid for a single trip within a period of five days. In the event the one-way trip cannot be completed within the valid life of the single-trip permit due to hazardous road conditions or vehicle breakdown, a one-day extension may be granted provided that the request is made to the DOT before the permit has expired. Permit restrictions are assigned based on requested dimensions and weights.
record.applicability_note: The gross weight is supplied, but the guidebook's bridge-formula note states that legal gross weight may be below 80,000 pounds depending on axle weights and spacing. Missing dimensions, load divisibility, permit status, and trip timing also prevent a permit determination.

source_text: 3. The vehicle height, length and width;
4. The axle configuration and weight over each axle;
5. The overall gross vehicle weight;
6. The dates of travel;

7. The details of the anticipated route of travel, including locations of the entrance to and exit from the New Jersey State highway system, including, but not limited to, the interstate highways, the New Jersey Turnpike, the Garden State Parkway south of Exit 105 and the Atlantic City Expressway; and
(d) Applications for single-trip permits will be reviewed for acceptability of the route being used in conjunction with the vehicle's load and axle configuration.

(e) Applications for single-trip permits will be rejected where the vehicle's load and axle configuration overstress the structures being crossed on the anticipated route of travel. Rejected applications will identify the structures on the proposed route being overstressed. Applicants can either modify the vehicle's load, weight over each axle or axle spacing to lessen the load impact or choose an alternative route. Applicants can contact the New Jersey Department of Transportation, Bureau of Structural Engineering at 609-530-2579 for assistance in the choice of acceptable alternative routes.

clauses: a) Any Drayage Truck that cannot be verified as compliant by reference to the Drayage Truck’s records in the DTR, or
b) Any Drayage Truck equipped with an engine of model year 1999 or older, or
c) Any Drayage Truck that is not an Alternative Truck as defined in SUBRULE 34-1060.

effective_2028_05_01.intro: Beginning May 1, 2028, at 12:01 AM, no Container Terminal Facility shall permit access into any Port Authority Terminal by:

record.label: SUBRULE 34-1100: REGISTRATION IN DRAYAGE TRUCK REGISTRY (DTR)
record.source_text: All Drayage Trucks seeking entry onto any Port Authority Terminal shall be registered in the DTR prior to the date of entry. Registration in the DTR shall be in electronic format via the PortTruckPass (PTP) website (www.porttruckpass.com). In the event of a change to the information provided for registration in the DTR with respect to a registered vehicle, such information shall be amended within ten (10) calendar days of the change via the PortTruckPass website (www.porttruckpass.com). Supporting documentation may be required for verification purposes with regard to registration or amendment.

nodes.label: SUBRULE 34-290: STATE LEGISLATION — Rules and Regulations Governing Traffic on Highways in Port Authority Air and Marine Terminals

record.label: SUBRULE 34-290: STATE LEGISLATION — Rules and Regulations Governing Traffic on Highways in Port Authority Air and Marine Terminals
source_text: All persons on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway must at all times comply with any lawful order, signal or direction by voice or hand of any member of the Port Authority police force. When traffic is controlled by traffic lights, signs or by mechanical or electrical signals, such lights, signs and signals shall be obeyed unless a Port Authority police officer directs otherwise.

Unless otherwise directed, all vehicles on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway shall at all times stay to the right of the center of the roadway, except in the case of one-way roadways; slow- moving vehicles shall remain as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the roadway; and where a roadway is marked with traffic lanes, vehicles shall not cross markings.

No person shall operate a motor vehicle on an air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless he is duly authorized to operate such vehicle on State and municipal highways in the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless he is especially authorized by the Port Authority to operate motor vehicles on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway. No motor vehicle shall be permitted on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless it is registered in accordance with the provisions of the law of the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless it is especially authorized by the Port Authority to be operated on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway.
